\section{Control-Flow Representation}
\label{app:replica}
\label{app:rewritten}
\label{app:rewritten_repair}
\label{app:replica_token_game}
% Former Appendix C (appendices/control_flow_replica.tex, no longer included), condensed on 19 Nov 2026.
% Sources: simulation_e3/runs/split13apr_20261106/{main,noguard,guard_orig,samelang}, runs/hm07_raw_20261111;
%   replica: process_discovery/ablation_silent_guard.py --reference train -> analysis/ablation_silent_guard_20261113.

Two controls examine how the representation of the control flow affects the
simulated visits. In the first, the languages of the three admissible nets were
encoded as state machines without silent transitions, with one place for each state
of the visit, after the languages of IM 0.0 and ILP 1.00 had been restricted to rules
3 and 5. Simulated with the settings of E3, the three state machines generate the
same distribution of sequences (sequence TVD 0.015 to the training log for all
three), although their precision ranges from 0.825 to 0.998. Behaviour that precision
counts against a net is hardly generated, because the routing is learned from the
observed visits. For HM 0.7, the state machine generates the same visits as the
discovered net. For IM 0.0, the representation decides. With the simple guard, its
discovered net generates 15.1\,\% visits without a stop and overlapping stops in
22.7\,\% of the multi-stop visits, while the state machine of the same language
generates none.

In the second control, ProSiT's routing was rebuilt as a token game without time
and resources, in which an enabled transition is drawn with a probability
proportional to its weight, as in stochastic labelled Petri nets
\cite{mannhardt2023stochasticProcessesModelling}. The weights
were estimated by counting on the aligned training log. The replica reproduces
ProSiT on the discovered IM 0.0 (15.7 against 15.1\,\% visits without a stop).
Adding the marking to the state of the weights removes every visit without a stop
and lowers the sequence TVD from 0.232 to 0.004. Each skip of a parallel branch is
thus learned on its own, without knowing whether another branch has already produced
a stop. In a state machine, and in a net without parallel branches such as HM 0.7,
every decision depends on the state anyway, so silent transitions alone are not the
cause. For a net with parallel branches, a guard on the number of stops gives every
truck its planned stops but does not repair how the stops are combined (sequence TVD
0.167, against 0.006 for the state machine). The counting estimator of the replica
is more flexible than ProSiT's trees, so the replica shows what the representation
allows, not what ProSiT learns.
